keyVerseText: Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered themselves together unto Jerusalem within three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month; and all the people sat in the street of the house of God, trembling because of this matter, and for the great rain. the great: Heb. the showers
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb רָעַד (râʻad) is a primitive root that fundamentally expresses the physical act of trembling or shaking. Its core sense involves a shuddering or quivering motion, whether mild or intense, extending even to the earth itself quaking. This literal sense of physical instability or movement underlines a tangible response to powerful forces, adding a vivid dimension beyond the simple English gloss of 'tremble.'
usageInScripture: With a total of four occurrences, רָעַד consistently conveys the idea of trembling or shaking, whether by people or the earth. The top translations emphasize 'trembling' twice and 'and it trembleth' once, indicating both human and environmental manifestations of this verb. This consistency in usage highlights its role in describing a physical and emotional reaction to awe-inspiring or fearsome circumstances.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding רָעַד enriches our grasp of biblical portrayals of reverence, fear, and divine power. The trembling it describes can reflect human responses to God's presence or judgment, reminding believers of their creaturely frailty before the Almighty. This verb also captures the earth's response to God's sovereignty, illustrating His control over creation. In the Christian faith, such trembling points us to a holy fear that leads to worship and trust in Christ, who holds all things together and calls us to stand firm in faith rather than fear.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 10:9 describes the people of Judah and Benjamin gathering and sitting 'in the street of the house of God, trembling because of this matter, and for the great rain.' Here, רָעַד conveys not only physical shaking but a deep emotional and spiritual response to the situation and divine providence. This trembling underscores the seriousness of the people's repentance and their awareness of God's hand in their circumstances, inviting us to consider how reverence and fear of the Lord shape communal and individual faith.
